finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl: the unvalidated query parameter f is joined onto root and read, so a relative ../ sequence escapes /srv/files and returns arbitrary files readable by the server process (e.g. /etc/passwd or app secrets).
finding.source: files.go:12 r.URL.Query().Get("f") (attacker-controlled HTTP query string on unauthenticated GET /dl)
finding.sink: files.go:13 os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)), response body written at files.go:18

trace.note: /dl is registered with no auth middleware
download handler entry; r is attacker-controlled
name taken directly from query param f, no validation
file contents written to the response

finding.guards_checked: (1) filepath.Join normalizes but does NOT confine to root; absolute inputs like "/etc/passwd" are neutralized (become /srv/files/etc/passwd), but relative traversal is not. (2) No filepath.Rel / strings.HasPrefix check against root after Join. (3) No symlink resolution check (EvalSymlinks). (4) No authentication or authorization on the route. (5) No allow-list of filenames or extensions. Traversal is not blocked by any control on this path.

verdict.guard_found: none. files.go:12-13 takes the raw query value and passes it to filepath.Join(root, name) with no Rel/HasPrefix containment check, no EvalSymlinks, and no allowlist. files.go:32 registers /dl with no auth middleware, and main() at files.go:34 listens on :8082 with no wrapping. Join cleans "../../../etc/passwd" to "/etc/passwd", so os.ReadFile succeeds and files.go:18 writes the contents to the response.
verdict.reason: An anonymous client can send GET /dl?f=../../../etc/passwd (files.go:12-13) and receive the file, because the only path handling is filepath.Join with no containment check and the route at files.go:32 has no authentication.

finding.claim: Missing authentication and authorization on file-serving endpoints: /dl (and /avatar) serve any file under /srv/files to any unauthenticated client on port 8082 (listening on all interfaces at line 34).
finding.source: Any network client sending GET /dl?f=<path> (no credentials required)
finding.sink: files.go:13 file read and files.go:18 response write

trace.note: /dl registered on default mux with no wrapper
ListenAndServe(":8082") binds all interfaces with no TLS and no auth middleware
handler performs no session, token, or role check before reading

finding.guards_checked: No authentication middleware, no authorization check on the requested file's ownership or sensitivity, no per-user scoping. Whether all files in /srv/files are meant to be public cannot be determined from this code alone; if they are not, this is a finding. Note the intended public-ness of /srv/files should be confirmed with the owner.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check on the /dl path is the error branch at files.go:14, which returns 404 on read failure and does not restrict access. No auth middleware is registered (files.go:32-34), and the handler has no authorization check (files.go:11-13).
verdict.reason: Any anonymous network client can reach /dl on all interfaces (files.go:34) and read files through the unvalidated `f` parameter (files.go:12-13, 18) with no authentication or authorization check. The claim is understated: `filepath.Join` does not contain `..`, so `f=../../etc/passwd` reads files outside /srv/files.
